rep.max: The chart shows the highest estimated 1RM achieved in each session. The top indicator shows your absolute personal record. This metric is useful for tracking your progression in terms of maximum strength.

descriptions.reps: This metric shows the total number of repetitions performed in each session. The top indicator shows the cumulative total of repetitions. It is useful for measuring the total volume of work performed and tracking your progression in terms of muscular endurance.

session.volume: Session volume is the total sum of weight lifted multiplied by repetitions across the entire training session. The chart shows this total for each day, and the top indicator shows your most intense session. This metric is excellent for measuring the overall intensity of your workouts.

set.volume: This metric represents the maximum volume achieved in a single set (weight × repetitions). The chart shows the highest value achieved in each session, while the top indicator shows your absolute personal record. It is useful for tracking the progression of your work capacity in individual sets.

descriptions.sets: The chart shows the number of sets completed on each training day. The top indicator shows the cumulative total of sets performed for this exercise. This metric helps you visualize the consistency and volume of your training over time.
descriptions.weight: The chart shows the maximum weight used in each training session, regardless of the repetitions performed. The top indicator shows the highest weight you have used. This metric is useful for tracking your progression in terms of absolute load.

markdown.dumbbells_kettlebells:
# **Dumbbells or Kettlebells**

When recording exercises with dumbbells or kettlebells, you must record the total weight lifted per repetition with both arms. For example, if each arm lifts 10 kg (≈22 lbs), your recorded weight should be 20 kg (≈44 lbs).
markdown.bars:
# **Bars (Any type of bar)**

When recording exercises with a bar, you must record the total weight lifted (including the bar). For example, if you lift a 20 kg bar with two 15 kg plates (one on each side), it should be recorded as 50 kg in total.
markdown.machines:
# **Machine**

When recording exercises on machines, you must record the weight indicated by the machine.
markdown.pulley:
# **Pulleys**

When recording pulley exercises, you must record the weight as follows:

- One pulley with both arms at the same time (e.g., tricep rope extension): record what the pulley indicates. If the pulley indicates 20 kg, record 20 kg.
- Two pulleys or one arm at a time on the same pulley (e.g., crossover or alternate curl): record the sum of both arms. 10 kg per arm (≈22 lbs) = 20 kg (≈44 lbs).
markdown.bodyweight:
# **Bodyweight (Bodyweight exercises)**

When recording bodyweight exercises, record the extra weight added. If you don't add weight, record 0.

1. Tap the keyboard icon (⌨️) to open the keyboard.

modals.best_set_content:
# 🏆 Your Best Set

Your best set is the combination of weight and repetitions that resulted in your **highest 1RM**.

It is calculated using: **Weight × (1 + Repetitions/30)**

This set determines your current rank in the exercise.
modals.stats_info_content:
# What are your statistics?

Here you can see how you have progressed in this exercise over time.

- **Graph:** Tap and hold on a point on the graph to see details for that day or session.
- **Tip:** Use this feature to better understand your evolution and motivate yourself to keep improving.
modals.target_set_content:
# 🎯 Target Set

The combination of weight and repetitions you need to complete to **move up to the next rank**.

It is calculated by adjusting the weight needed to reach the next level threshold, while keeping the same repetitions.

**Tip:** Increase weight gradually while maintaining good technique.

dumbbells.content: When recording exercises with dumbbells or kettlebells, you must record the total weight lifted per repetition with both arms. For example, if each arm lifts 10 kg (≈22 lbs), your recorded weight should be 20 kg (≈44 lbs).

bars.title: Bars (Any type of bar)

machines.title: Machine
machines.content: On machine exercises, log the weight the machine shows.

pulleys.title: Pulleys
pulleys.content:
On pulley exercises, the weight you log depends on how you use it:

- One pulley with both arms at once (e.g. triceps rope pushdown): record what the pulley shows. If the pulley shows 20 kg, record 20 kg.
- Two pulleys or one arm at a time on the same pulley (e.g. crossover or alternate curl): record the sum of both arms. 10 kg per arm (≈22 lbs) = 20 kg (≈44 lbs).

bodyweight.content: When logging bodyweight exercises, only log the extra weight added. If you don't add weight, leave it empty.

bands.title: Resistance Bands

how_to_keyboard.title: How to use the virtual keyboard?

2. Enter the exact weight in the "Weight" field (using a dot or comma for decimals).
3. Enter the number of repetitions in the "Reps" field.
4. Tap "Confirm" to save your data.

help.todays_session:
# How is today's workout calculated?

Symmetry determines your workout for today based on your current training plan:

## 1. Today's session
If you have a scheduled session for today in your training plan, that will be your recommended session.

## 2. Nearest pending session
If there's no session for today, the first uncompleted session from previous days in your plan will be shown.

## 3. Next available session
If you've completed all previous sessions, the next available session in your plan will be shown.

## 4. No active plan
If you don't have an active training plan, you can generate a session with AI or create an empty session.

**Tip:** Keep your training plan updated to get the best recommendations.
help.new_training:
# New Workout

You have two options to start a new workout:

## **Generate Workout with AI**
Our artificial intelligence will create a personalized session based on:
- Your workout history
- Your current goals
- Your available equipment
- Your experience level

## **Empty Workout**
Start with a blank session where you can:
- Add exercises on the go
- Create spontaneous workouts
- Try new exercises
- Train without a specific plan

**Recommendation:** Use AI for structured workouts and empty workout for flexible sessions.

plan_config.title: Settings

si_card.heading: Ask me for anything and I'll adjust it
si_card.example: “This week I only want to train 3 days”

selector.empty: No options are available right now.

split.question: How do you want to split your workouts?
split.recovery_description: Each day you train the most rested muscles. The AI decides the split every week.
split.ppl_description: The classic. Three session types on rotation.
split.upper_lower_description: You alternate upper and lower body.
split.full_body_description: Your whole body every session. Good if you train few days.
split.lower_focus_description: More leg volume than upper body.

goal.question: What do you want to get out of training?
goal.build_muscle_description: Volume and progression aimed at growing.
goal.conditioning_description: Shorter rests and more work per session.
goal.general_fitness_description: A balanced plan to stay in shape.

duration.question: How long do you want each session to be?

experience.question: How much training experience do you have?
experience.beginner_description: Less than a year training consistently.
experience.intermediate_description: One to three years, and you know the technique.
experience.advanced_description: Years of training and you know what works for you.

variety.question: How much do you want your exercises to change?
variety.consistent_description: Almost always the same exercises, to track progress.
variety.balanced_description: A stable base with some rotation.

rep_ranges.question: How many reps per set?
rep_ranges.auto_description: The AI picks the range for each exercise.

progression.question: What should go up week to week?
progression.auto_description: The AI decides what to progress on each exercise.
progression.load_description: Same reps, a bit more weight.

training_days.question: Which days do you want to train?
training_days.help: Pick at least one day. Symmetry Intelligence distributes your sessions across them.

muscles.question: Which muscles do you want to work on?
muscles.question_excluded: Which muscles should the plan work around?
muscles.tap_and_turn_hint: Tap the muscles to pick them, and turn the body around to see the back.
muscles.limit_reached: You can pick up to {max} muscles.
muscles.blocked_hint: Muscles in grey are already in {list}.
muscles.blocked_tap: {name} is already in {list}. Take it out from there to add it here.

equipment.question: Where do you train?
equipment.help: The plan only uses exercises you can actually do there.
equipment.commercial_gym_description: Machines, cables, racks and full free weights.
equipment.small_gym_description: Dumbbells, barbells and a few benches.
equipment.calisthenics_description: Bodyweight, a pull-up bar and bands.

injuries.question: Do you have any injuries?
injuries.help: The plan works around them. Add the area and, if you want, what happens to you.
injuries.note_hint: For example: it only hurts on deep flexion

sets.question: How many sets per exercise?
sets.help: Compound lifts and isolation work usually need different set counts.
sets.auto_description: The AI picks the sets for each exercise.
sets.manual_description: You choose how many sets each type gets.

confirm.title: Rebuild your intelligent plan now?
confirm.body: Workouts you've already completed won't be touched.
confirm.next_week_done: Saved. Your plan will use your changes from next week.

plan_config.discard_body: The changes you made to your plan won't be applied.

error.load_failed: We couldn't load your plan's settings.
error.save_failed: We couldn't save your changes. Your plan hasn't changed.

exercises.promoted_question: Which exercises do you want to see more of?
exercises.promoted_help: The plan will reach for these whenever they fit the session.
exercises.excluded_question: Which exercises do you want to avoid?
exercises.excluded_help: The plan will never use these. It always finds a replacement.
exercises.limit_reached: You can add up to {max} exercises.
exercises.blocked_one: {name} is already in {list}. Take it out from there to add it here.
exercises.blocked_many: {count} exercises are already in {list}, so they were not added.

smart_plan.ai_body: I've adjusted it after your last workout: more press, less leg volume.
